narration: Sometimes one coding agent can handle the whole task. Sometimes the job is easier to split into independent pieces.
captionText: It depends on how the work can be divided.
voiceDirection: Neutral opening. Do not imply multi-agent is always better.

narration: In a multi-agent workflow, one main agent keeps the goal, then delegates bounded work to subagents with their own focused context.
For a coding task, those subagents might independently research the codebase, build a frontend change, inspect backend logic, and prepare tests.
voiceDirection: Give each role a distinct beat.

narration: Because those workstreams are independent, they can progress in parallel instead of one agent completing every step sequentially.
captionText: Separate work can reduce wall-clock time.

narration: The important part is coordination. The main agent has to know what each subagent owns, what result it should return, and when to wait.
If several agents edit the same files or depend on each other step by step, parallel work can create conflicts instead of speed.
Use subagents for independent, bounded tasks. Keep short tasks and tightly dependent steps with the main agent.
captionText: Split by independence, not by hype.

narration: So multi-agent coding is not an AI team replacing humans. It is an orchestration pattern: divide focused work, run useful parts in parallel, then bring the results back for integration and review.
